findings.evidence: suite_changes.diff shows `expect(violations).toEqual([])` deleted from the generated R10 ordering test with no reason in the envelope (departures: []). It was the suite's only enforcement of R10's ranking contract; my probe shows the delivered code PASSES that assertion as written (3-member WORLD_TEAM can never tie: max sleeping score 51⅔ < min awake 60), so the removal was unnecessary as well as unexplained — and it let the real APAC/4-member ordering defect ship green.

blocking: R10 ordering defect: apps/app/domain/recommender.ts:42-45 sorts by score only, so when a sleeping slot and an all-awake slot tie in score (V49 and V48 both = 60) the start-time tie-break ranks the sleeping slot above the awake one. Verified user-visible in the rendered panel (team [America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, Asia/Singapore, America/St_Johns] @120m: recommendation #1 is 'disruptive (60), 1 sleeping' above #3 'compromise (60), 0 sleeping') and at the API level for the shipped APAC Triangle preset at all six durations. Fix: sort key must be (slot has a sleeping member, score desc, startUtc). Answer-key gap in the same item: no V row pins R10's ordering — the builder must propose V74 (e.g.: for the LA/NY/Singapore/St_Johns team at 120m on 2025-06-18, no slot containing a sleeping member ranks above any zero-sleeping slot, and the top slot is 2025-06-18T23:00:00Z compromise).

Unexplained weakening of the generated suite: `expect(violations).toEqual([])` — the only executable enforcement of R10's zero-sleeping-first ranking — was deleted from apps/app/tests/generated/bcca0d92.test.ts with no reason given. The delivered code passes that assertion as written (probe /tmp/r10_order_probe.ts), so the removal was unnecessary as well as unexplained. Restore it AND extend it to a 4-member team where the 60/60 tie is live: with the 3-member WORLD_TEAM a tie is impossible (max sleeping score 51⅔ < min awake 60), so the restored assertion alone would still test nothing.
